answer: An agent market requires a separate escrow bond for every identity bidding on jobs, whether mapping a cliff ledge, tracking dune erosion, or tending an orchard. Bonds stay locked until an audit window closes, and a contract slashes the bond when a challenger submits verifiable proof of a false result. Spawning identities creates no free capacity: an attacker must lock more capital for each one and risks losing it on fraudulent work.
